exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
usage:
  goal up [--compose]                             start PostgreSQL and RustFS, prepare the database roles,
                                                  migrate the database, prepare the bucket, start the egress
                                                  proxy, run goald (and, with sign-in, Mailpit and the auth
                                                  service); --compose runs goald and the auth service as
                                                  compose services too, and returns once they are healthy
  goal run <factory> "<brief>" [--type T] [--body B] [--priority N] [--detach]
                                                  submit a work item and follow it until a human or done
                                                  (--type: one of the factory's work types; default its
                                                  first, none when it declares none)
  goal follow <item>                              follow an item's events again
  goal item <item>                                show an item with its outputs as JSON, and its human
                                                  touches (who acted, where, planned or not, why) on stderr
  goal approve <item>                             approve an item waiting at a human station
  goal reject <item> --reason "..."               send it back for rework
  goal retry <item>                               send a blocked item back to its station's queue
  goal merge <item>                               merge the item's pull request, then approve it
                                                  (at a station with action: merge)
  goal note <item> "<text>"                       leave a note for the agents: the item's next run
                                                  reads it
  goal move <item> <station> [--reason "..."]     put the item at another station (a reason is needed
                                                  upstream, where it counts as rework); a run in
                                                  progress is stopped
  goal pause <item> [--reason "..."]              stop the item where it is (goal retry resumes it);
                                                  a run in progress is stopped
  goal status [--factory F] [--window 7d]         per factory over the last days (1d to 90d): work in
                                                  progress, items done, lead time p85, human touches per
                                                  finished item, the touchless share and the station with
                                                  the most unplanned touches; without --factory, every
                                                  factory and the organization's total
  goal andon <factory>                            whether the line runs, its gates' rework tallies and
                                                  the recent andon pulls
  goal andon pull <factory> --reason "..."        pull the andon cord: the line releases and claims
                                                  nothing until it is cleared
  goal andon clear <factory> [--note "..."]       clear it: the line runs again
  goal factory pull <factory> <dir> [--version N|current|draft]
                                                  write a version's files (default: the current one)
                                                  into a new folder, with .goal/pulled.json
  goal factory validate <dir>... [--offline]      validate folders through goald (--offline: schema and
                                                  references only, without goald; goal validate is
                                                  goal factory validate --offline, same flags)
  goal factory push <dir> [--publish [--message M]] [--replace-draft] [--force] [--move S=T]...
                                                  make the folder the factory's draft (creating the
                                                  factory if its metadata.id is new); --publish then
                                                  publishes it. Refused when an open draft has changes
                                                  the folder was not pulled from (--replace-draft
                                                  archives it) or a version was published after the
                                                  pull (--force pushes over it)
  goal factory publish <factory> [--message M] [--move S=T]...
                                                  validate and publish the open draft
  goal factory list [--validate] [--archived]     the factories: current version, open draft, paused
                                                  (--archived: only the archived ones)
  goal factory versions <factory>                 the published versions (* the one that runs)
  goal factory restore <factory> <N> [--move S=T]...
                                                  run version N again
  goal factory archive <factory>                  retire a paused factory none of whose items is being
                                                  worked; it keeps its history and leaves the list
  goal factory restore <factory>                  list an archived factory again; it stays paused
  goal factory delete <factory> [--yes]           delete an archived factory for good, with its items,
                                                  runs and versions, after typing its name (--yes: no
                                                  prompt); a factory never published needs no archive
  goal org list                                   the organizations (* the one commands act in)
  goal org use <slug>                             act in this organization from now on (config file)
  goal org create <slug> --name N [--mark M]      create an organization (platform admins only)
  goal org update <slug> [--name N] [--slug S] [--mark M] [--max-slots N]
                                                  rename it, or cap the agents running at once
                                                  across its factories (--max-slots 0: no cap)
  goal org delete <slug> [--yes]                  delete it after typing its name (--yes: no prompt);
                                                  it is purged after GOAL_ORG_RETENTION
  goal key list                                   the organization's API keys: hint, scopes, factories,
                                                  ceiling, expiry, last use
  goal key create <name> --scope S [--scope S]... [--factory F]... [--role viewer|approver|editor] [--expires 90d]
                                                  create an API key for scripts and CI (scopes: permissions
                                                  such as org:read, factory:read, item:create; --role is
                                                  the most it acts as on a factory, default viewer;
                                                  --expires 1d to 90d, default 90d). The secret is printed
                                                  once, alone on stdout: store it as GOAL_API_KEY
  goal key revoke <name|id>                       revoke a key: anything using it stops working at once
  goal connection list [--kind K] [--factory F]   the organization's connections: kind, status, which
                                                  secrets are set (never a value), what uses them
  goal connection show <name>                     one connection: its fields, last test, the env names a
                                                  run gets and its kind's docs
  goal connection create <name> --kind K [--field k=v]... [--secret k=-] [--secret-file k=<path>]... [--description D]
                                                  create a connection (owners and admins); a secret comes
                                                  from stdin (k=-, one value) or a file, never argv
  goal connection update <name> [--name N] [--description D] [--field k=v]... [--secret k=-] [--secret-file k=<path>]...
                                                  rename it, change its fields (merged; k= clears one) or
                                                  replace the named secrets
  goal connection delete <name>                   delete it (refused while a factory's current version
                                                  names it)
  goal connection test <name>                     run its kind's test from goald (exit 1 when it fails)
  goal connection kinds                           the kinds connections are made of, the platform's and
                                                  the organization's
  goal connection kind push <file.yaml>           create or replace an organization kind from its file
  goal connection kind delete <name>              delete an organization kind no connection is of
  goal credential list                            the organization's credentials: type, factories, what uses
                                                  them, last use and expiry (never a value)
  goal credential create <name> --type T [--description D] [--factory <id>]... [--all-factories] [--expires YYYY-MM-DD] [--remind-days N]
                                                  create a credential (owners and admins; types api_key,
                                                  oauth_token, ssh_key, cloud_role, app_key); its value
                                                  comes from stdin, never argv: ... < value-file
  goal credential replace <name>                  replace its value with the one on stdin
  goal credential rm <name>                       delete it (refused while a connection refers to it as
                                                  {{name}}; the error names them)
  goal credential import <file> [--format env|yaml] [--on-conflict replace|skip] [--dry-run]
                                                  import a .env or YAML file's credentials (format from
                                                  the extension by default; a name that exists is skipped
                                                  unless --on-conflict replace); prints each name as new
                                                  or exists (--dry-run) or what was done with it
  goal knowledge sources [--factory F]            the knowledge base's sources: kind, status, documents,
                                                  last and next sync, the factories that search them
  goal knowledge add <name> --kind upload|synced|live [--connection C] [--config k=v]... [--title T] [--every 1h]
                                                  add a source (owners and admins); a synced or live one
                                                  reads a connection, --config says what (space=ENG)
  goal knowledge sync <source>                    sync it now
  goal knowledge upload <source> <file>...        upload text, Markdown, HTML, JSON or YAML files to an
                                                  upload source; indexed at its next sync
  goal knowledge documents <source>               its documents: id, title, status, size
  goal knowledge rm <document>                    delete an uploaded document
  goal knowledge search "<query>" [--source S]... [--limit N]
                                                  search as agents do: the best passages first, with
                                                  their document ids or links
  goal search "<query>" [--limit N] [--json]      search the organization's items, agents, factories
                                                  and connections, by group, best first (--limit: per
                                                  group, 1 to 20, default 5; --json: goald's answer as
                                                  it came)
  goal runs [--factory F] [--status S] [--since T] [--until T] [--search Q] [--limit N] [--cursor C] [--json]
                                                  the organization's agent runs, newest first: factory,
                                                  item, station, agent, model, start, duration, turns,
                                                  cost and status, then the window's totals and spend
                                                  (--since/--until: RFC 3339, default the current UTC
                                                  day; --status: running, succeeded, failed or
                                                  cancelled; --search: item title, agent, model or
                                                  #147; another page prints its --cursor)
  goal eval run [--case C] [--draft] [--factory F] [--json]
                                                  start an eval run of the factory's eval cases (every
                                                  one, or --case), on the current version or --draft,
                                                  and print what it is about to cost
  goal eval show <run> [--factory F] [--json]     an eval run's state and cost, and each case's tries:
                                                  pass, fail or error
  goal spend [--window week|month|90d] [--json]   what the organization's agent runs cost (default this
                                                  week), per merged item and on rework, and each
                                                  factory's budget: running, stopped or over_budget,
                                                  its spend today and in the last 7 days
  goal triggers list <factory> [--json]           the factory's triggers in definition order: on or off,
                                                  when they fire, what they create, the items they
                                                  created in the last 7 days, and why one may not be
                                                  creating items (triggers change in the definition)
  goal triggers show <factory> <trigger> [--json] a trigger, what its items did in the last 7 days
                                                  and its recent events: created, merged or skipped
  goal webhooks list <factory> [--json]           the factory's webhook endpoints: kind, address,
                                                  the triggers they feed, deliveries in 7 days
                                                  (never a secret)
  goal webhooks create <factory> <name> [--kind generic|github] [--json]
                                                  add an endpoint (default kind generic); its signing
                                                  secret is printed once, alone on stdout: store it in
                                                  the sender now
  goal webhooks rotate <factory> <name> [--json]  replace its signing secret, printed once the same
                                                  way; the old one stops working at once
  goal webhooks deliveries <factory> <name> [--limit N] [--after C] [--json]
                                                  what it received, newest first: refused (and why),
                                                  accepted or created an item
  goal connection import-env                      once, after the cutover to connections: GOAL_GITHUB_TOKEN
                                                  becomes github, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
                                                  claude; names that exist are left as they are
  goal storage init                               create the bucket if missing
  goal catalog skills sync --file <sources.yaml> [--search <q>]... [--top <n>]
                                                  fetch skills.sh skills (a YAML list of
                                                  owner/repo@skill[#commit], plus the top n of each
                                                  search) into the bucket's skills catalog
  goal catalog skills list [q]                    the catalog's skills: key, commit, installs
  goal catalog templates push <dir> --version N [--name NAME]
                                                  add a template version (<dir>/template.yaml and the
                                                  definition in <dir>/factory/; NAME defaults to the
                                                  folder's name) to the bucket's template catalog
  goal catalog templates list                     the catalog's templates, latest version of each
  goal db init                                    create the database roles goald runs as (goal_owner,
                                                  goal_app) and hand the schema to goal_owner
  goal db migrate                                 apply the pending migrations as goal_owner
                                                  (GOAL_MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL), as goald does at its start
  goal db recover-admin <email>                   make the person a platform admin with database access
                                                  alone (GOAL_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL), creating them if no
                                                  one has the email; goald may be stopped
  goal db recover-owner <org> <email>             make the person an owner of the organization, the same way
  goal db rekey                                   reseal every connection under the active master key (the
                                                  first of GOAL_MASTER_KEYS) as goal_owner; then drop old keys
  goal admin list                                 the platform admins (platform admins only)
  goal admin add <email>                          make a person who has signed in a platform admin
  goal admin remove <email>                       stop them being one (the last one stays)
  goal admin events [--kind K] [--before N]       the security log, newest first
  goal login [--store keychain|file]              sign the CLI in: approve the code it shows at
                                                  <goald>/device in a browser; the session goes to the
                                                  OS keychain, or with --store file (remembered) to
                                                  credentials.json beside the config file (mode 0600)
  goal login --token [--store keychain|file]      store a personal token (or API key) read from stdin
                                                  instead: goal login --token < token-file
  goal logout [--all]                             end the CLI's session (--all: every session of yours)
                                                  and forget it here
  goal whoami                                     who the CLI acts as, and in which organizations
  goal version                                    print the module version and build info

<item> is goal#2 (factory and number), the item's id, or a bare number such as 2 when one
factory has that item (--factory F picks the factory of a bare number). <factory> is a name or an id.
--move S=T sends the open items of station S, which the new version drops, to station T.

Factory definitions live in goald (drafts and published versions), not in files: goal factory
push is how a folder changes one, and goald ignores factory files written to the bucket.

Every command that talks to goald (run, follow, item, note, move, pause, the decisions, status, andon, factory, connection, credential, knowledge, search, runs, eval, spend, triggers, webhooks) acts in one
organization: --org <slug|id>, else GOAL_ORG, else org in the config file
($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/goal/config.json, default ~/.config/goal/config.json; goal org use writes it),
else the install's only organization (decisions are the local user's); with GOAL_API_KEY set, or a key or
personal token stored by goal login --token, commands act in its own organization

With sign-in on (GOAL_AUTH=session), commands send GOAL_API_KEY (an API key goal_sk_… or a
personal token goal_pat_…) when it is set, else what goal login stored for goald's origin, and
only over https or to this machine; a refused credential or permission exits 77
